author: NorthEast News Desk
body: Two 17-year-old boys were arrested after gunfire struck homes in New Bedford’s West End, police said Thursday. No injury to the intended target was reported.

Officers went to the intersection of Chestnut and Willis streets at about 3:30 p.m. Wednesday following reports of shots. They found spent cartridge casings and damage to several nearby houses. Investigators allege that two masked teenagers fired toward a person in the area before leaving the scene.

Police located the teenagers inside a nearby home and recovered two firearms believed to have been used in the shooting. Detectives also seized ammunition, clothing, masks, a 3D printer and a handgun frame that investigators believe was produced with the printer.

Both teenagers face charges that include assault with intent to murder, carrying a loaded firearm without a license and intentionally firing near a building and causing property damage. One also faces allegations tied to manufacturing a firearm with a 3D printer. The accusations remain charges, and the source report did not identify the juveniles.
dek: Police said the intended target was not hurt and investigators recovered two firearms, ammunition and a handgun frame believed to be 3D-printed.
headline: Two teens arrested after gunfire damages New Bedford homes
